questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

What would be one indicator of productive inefficiency in an economy?

options.A: an excess of imports over exports
options.B: prices in excess of marginal costs
options.C: rationing of certain goods and services
options.D: unemployment due to deficient aggregate demand

options.A: the financing of investment largely by the issue of bonds
options.B: the opportunity for managers to buy shares at a reduced price
options.C: the payment of high dividends to shareholders

options.A: to improve management control and co-ordination
options.B: to reduce costs by exploiting economies of scale
options.C: to satisfy the ambitions of senior management
options.D: to secure greater pricing power by increasing its market dominance

A firm operates in a contestable market. How is the firm likely to decide on the price of its product?

options.A: It will set a price equal to minimum average cost.
options.B: It will set a price to deter the entry of new firms.
options.C: It will set a price to maximise its revenue.
options.D: It will set a price to maximise sales in the short run.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve faced by an individual firm in an oligopolistic industry. P price 1 O Q quantity What explains the shape of the curve?

options.A: lack of productive capacity at output levels greater than Q
options.B: the ability of the firm to practise price discrimination
options.C: the absence of barriers to new firms entering the industry
options.D: the response of rival firms to changes in its price

questions.questionText: How does monopolistic competition differ from perfect competition?

options.A: Average revenue can be greater than average cost in the long run.
options.B: Average revenue can be greater than average cost in the short run.

questions.questionText: Which measure to reduce the abuse of monopoly power is an example of regulation?

options.A: legislation to forbid price fixing by cartels

questions.questionText: What are the losses in economic efficiency that are likely to result from a policy of income redistribution from the rich to the poor? distortion of individual administrative costs disincentive choices between work of the redistribution effects and leisure policy

A firm is faced with a shortage of labour. It decides to introduce its own training scheme for school leavers. What effect is this most likely to have on the firm?

options.A: a decrease in the number that it employs
options.B: a decrease in the productivity of its workforce
options.C: an increase in the geographical mobility of its labour
options.D: a shift of the supply curve for its labour to the right

questions.questionText: Recently, among European countries the Netherlands had the highest percentage of part-time employees and an average working week for all employees of 32 hours. Greece had a smaller percentage of part-time employees but an average working week for all employees of 41 hours. Which conclusion may be drawn from this information?

options.A: Greece has a higher percentage of its workforce in full-time employment than the Netherlands.
options.B: On average part-time employees work longer in Greece than in the Netherlands.
options.C: The average working week in Greece for full-time employees is longer than in the Netherlands.
options.D: There are more part-time employees in the Netherlands than in Greece.

questions.questionText: What is the most likely reason that a rise in the savings ratio of a country may increase its rate of development in the long run?

options.A: It would encourage a shift of resources from the secondary to the primary sector.
options.B: It would free resources for the production of capital goods.
options.C: It would increase the level of international trade.
options.D: It would increase the rate of interest.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the most accurate statement about developing economies?

options.A: A dependence on primary products for export revenues means that developing countries are reliant on the industrialised world for their economic performance.
options.B: High levels of capital per head mean that they must rely on overseas trade if they are to achieve higher growth rates.
options.C: High real GDP per head, plus high rates of population growth, reduce their ability to increase their standard of living.
options.D: Migration of labour from rural to urban areas is of significance only if it results in labour shortages in the rural economy.
